blocks.title: Why it's said this way — one clue, one choice

segments.text: ਸਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਅਕਾਲ is specifically a Sikh greeting. ਨਮਸਤੇ is the broader greeting taught here. Do not guess a person's community from a Punjabi name. For a named reader whose Sikh context is not stated, choose ਨਮਸਤੇ.
Imagine a note to Manan. Point to the broader opening, then copy it once in Gurmukhi: ਨਮਸਤੇ. Keep the last vowel sign attached to its letter.
One context choice is enough. The next tiny step places the reader's name.

feedback.correct: The broader taught greeting fits a reader whose community is not specified.
feedback.incorrect: Choose the broader greeting here, not a community-specific one; then copy its Gurmukhi form.

blocks.title: Why it's said this way — a promise, not a second hello

Copy the everyday ending once: ਫਿਰ ਮਿਲਾਂਗੇ (phir milāṁge)। (sentence boundary) Notice the word space and the mark after the final word. You are not assembling a message yet.

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Close all earlier pages. You already know the short pieces needed for a note. This time there is no sentence bank or sample to reproduce.

As Manan, write Aman a 30–40-word Gurmukhi message. Greet Aman and ask how he is. Identify yourself as Manan. Include the already taught liking for water and at least one other familiar interest. Put your own wellbeing reply after the interest sentence or sentences. Suggest meeting again and close. Choose any additional familiar fact you need to reach the word band. Do not reopen a page or use a dictionary, translator, or spell-checker before finishing your draft.

There is no exam clock. Write one short block, pause, and continue. The earlier supported model went from Aman to Manan, did not include the water liking, and put the wellbeing reply earlier. Recalling it unchanged cannot meet this new task.

blocks.title: Guided Practice — self-check after the draft

segments.text: Count space-separated words and keep the result between 30 and 40. Check one dimension at a time: the named reader and appropriate tone; meaning and sentence order; agreement; spacing; Gurmukhi spelling; then punctuation. Only after recording those checks may you reopen earlier pages to repair a word. A different well-formed message can be valid; no single exact string is the answer to free composition.
Record the word count and one repair you made. This untimed checkpoint does not award timed-paper credit or whole-A1 readiness; two complete mocks and human validation remain separate work.
